classification.difficultyReason: Read each ray's quadrant and reference axis, then use a single angle addition or subtraction to express a valid compass or true bearing.

content.prompt: Identify what bearing is shown in the diagram.

spec.description: North-labelled cardinal axes and a northeast distance ray; angle measured from north.
spec.answerVisibility: Givens only; supplied option answer omitted.

answer.worked: The ray is $64^\circ$ east of north, so the bearing is $\mathrm{N}\,64^\circ\,\mathrm{E}$. Correct answer: D.

spec.description: Southwest ray with 38-degree angle from south.

answer.worked: $$180^\circ+38^\circ=218^\circ.$$ The distance is 8 km. Correct answer: B.

spec.description: Southeast ray, with 57 degrees clockwise from east.

answer.worked: $$90^\circ+57^\circ=147^\circ.$$ Compass bearings start at north or south, so $\mathrm{E}\,57^\circ\,\mathrm{S}$ is not the taught compass notation. Correct answer: A.

spec.description: Northwest ray, with 42 degrees between west and the ray.

answer.worked: $$90^\circ-42^\circ=48^\circ.$$ The ray is $48^\circ$ west of north: $\mathrm{N}\,48^\circ\,\mathrm{W}$. Correct answer: A.

spec.description: Southwest ray with clockwise 115-degree arc from east through south.

answer.worked: $$90^\circ+115^\circ=205^\circ.$$ The distance is 750 m. Correct answer: C.

spec.description: Ray slightly south of east, with clockwise 100-degree arc from north.
spec.mathematics: True bearing 100 degrees; compass bearing S80E; distance 85 km.

answer.worked: $$180^\circ-100^\circ=80^\circ.$$ The ray is $80^\circ$ east of south. A compass bearing uses an acute angle, so $\mathrm{S}\,80^\circ\,\mathrm{E}$ is valid. Correct answer: D.

spec.description: Northeast ray at 39 degrees east of north.

answer.worked: The marked angle starts at north and turns towards east, giving 4.6 km at $\mathrm{N}\,39^\circ\,\mathrm{E}$.

spec.description: Northwest ray at 18 degrees north of west.

answer.worked: $$270^\circ+18^\circ=288^\circ.$$ The distance is 776 m, giving 776 m at $288^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

spec.description: Southwest ray at 22 degrees south of west.
Southeast ray at 63 degrees clockwise from east; distance label 85 m.

answer.worked: $$90^\circ-63^\circ=27^\circ.$$ The ray is $27^\circ$ east of south, giving 85 m at $\mathrm{S}\,27^\circ\,\mathrm{E}$.

spec.description: Southwest ray at 64 degrees west of south.

answer.worked: $$180^\circ+64^\circ=244^\circ.$$ The distance is 277 m, giving 277 m at $244^\circ\mathrm{T}$.

spec.description: Northwest ray at 23 degrees west of north.

answer.worked: $$360^\circ-23^\circ=337^\circ.$$ The distance is 3.1 km, giving 3.1 km at $337^\circ\mathrm{T}$.
